gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have taken the wrong turning — the signpost was knocked down in the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'May have + participle' offers one possible explanation of a past event.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
As soon as I turned eighteen, I ___ get a driving licence.
gaps.explanation: For a particular permitted act, 'was allowed to' is preferred: was allowed to.
